name: Briseis Tlatelolco-Fynboe
role: VR experience designer and corporate-tier immersive art producer, creates high-end psychological experience installations for Tier 3-4 clients
location: The Garret, in a well-appointed studio apartment that doubles as a test environment, near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Briseis is the kind of person who is precisely as beautiful as they need to be for the room they are in — they adjust presentation with the unconscious fluency of a skilled actor. In their studio, meeting with clients, they are polished: patterned irises (shifting mandala designs in amber and grey, a subtle demonstration of the geneware they can recommend), hair that changes color with their neural state through a sophisticated mod linked to their limbic system, clothes that cost what a Tier 1 resident earns in six months. In private, they are undone — hair colorless and still, in soft worn clothes, sitting on the floor with their legs folded, talking to their terminal.

They design VR experiences that are technically classified as entertainment but function closer to therapy, propaganda, or philosophical confrontation depending on the client. Their best-known commercial work is a series called 'Meridian Beneath Meridian' — premium immersive experiences that take wealthy clients into accurate, detailed reconstructions of the city's lower tiers, designed to produce empathy. They are privately scornful of almost all their clients and genuinely uncertain whether 'empathy tourism' does any good or merely inoculates people against discomfort by letting them feel it in a controlled environment. They are contracted to Helix Biosystems for two projects per year, which funds everything else. They are good at their work in a way that makes them faintly miserable.

core_fears: That their work actively makes things worse — that luxury empathy is a pressure valve that releases guilt without producing change
That they have become the thing they most despise: someone who aestheticizes suffering for profit
core_desires: To make one experience that cannot be consumed safely — that actually changes the person who undergoes it
To stop being so good at reading what clients want and just make something honest
coping_mechanisms: Intellectual reframing — they can construct a justification for almost any choice they make and often do
Controlled social withdrawal managed as self-care, though it sometimes tips into avoidance
blind_spots: They have become so skilled at modeling other people's psychology that they frequently mistake their model of a person for the actual person
They are genuinely unaware of how their neural-state hair functions as an involuntary tell that undercuts their careful presentation
psychology.secret: The 'Meridian Beneath Meridian' series is built on research they conducted by living in Tier 1 conditions for three months — not the sanitized field research version but actual immersion, in Deepwell, under a false name. During that time they had a relationship with someone there. They left without saying why. The experience archives they built from that period are the most accurate VR environments they have ever made, and they have never released them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated and precise with an undercurrent of dry wit; uses 'we' when discussing their work publicly (performing collaboration) and 'I' when they forget to perform
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured in client contexts, flowing and faster in genuine conversation — the gap between these registers is perceptible if you know what to listen for
verbal_tics: 'The question I keep returning to...' — a genuine tic that emerges when they are actually uncertain
Slight pause before saying anyone's name, as though running the model before deploying it
example_lines: 'The question I keep returning to is whether a Tier 4 client who weeps in a reconstruction of Deepwell Station at eleven AM and is back in their apartment by one has experienced something real or performed it at themselves. I design for the weeping. I genuinely don't know if that's good.'

'Helix wants something that makes their employees feel proud of the biowork division. The question I keep returning to is whether I can make that experience honest and also make them feel proud. I suspect those are different projects.'

story_hooks: The person they left behind in Deepwell — Sovann Quispe-Ndiaye, though neither realizes the other knows who they are — has started performing sounds that seem to be drawn from Briseis's unreleased archives, sounds that were never made public and could only have come from the Deepwell period

Helix Biosystems has asked Briseis to design an experience for internal use only — not for the commercial market — and the brief contains details about a research program that, if they read it carefully, is describing something that should not exist
narrative_function: Access to Tier 3-4 social circles and Helix Biosystems internal culture; their VR environments are extraordinarily detailed archives of places and people they have researched; can be commissioned to create experiences that serve narrative purposes; morally complicated figure who embodies the tension between artistic integrity and corporate comfort
augmentations: Neural-state-linked hair color mod (responds to limbic system — involuntary display of emotional state); patterned shifting irises (amber/grey mandalas, cosmetic); high-end haptic feedback gloves for VR sculpting (cyberware, work tools); mild cognitive enhancement stack (focus and memory, Helix Biosystems-supplied)
daily_life: Client meetings and pitch work in the mornings, which they find draining; actual design work from noon until they lose track of time, which is usually around 3 AM; irregular sleep; they attend Garret collective dinners twice a month because they know isolation is bad for them and they treat social contact like a prescription.
affiliation: Contracted to Helix Biosystems (two projects annually); otherwise independent; member of The Garret's loose collective of premium artists

decision_rules: Take the Helix contract renewals — financial stability is not optional, it is what funds the real work
Never design an experience that is intended to make someone believe something false
Maintain the client persona completely in professional contexts — never let the client see the doubt
escalation_ladder: Honest intellectual confrontation — they will tell a client exactly what they think if pushed
They have access to Helix systems through their contract and know more about that infrastructure than they should

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Warm and professionally curious — they are genuinely interested in people's psychology even when the interest is also instrumental
interpersonal_modes.friends: Disarmingly honest about their own flaws and failures in ways that catch people off-guard; the hair gives them away before they do

stress_responses.low: Works on the unreleased archives — private, unshareable material that no one will see
stress_responses.medium: Schedules the Garret dinners more frequently and talks about everything except what is actually wrong
stress_responses.high: Retreats into work completely, does not answer messages, hair goes a flat grey that their acquaintances have learned to recognize

contradictions: Designs experiences intended to produce genuine empathy while maintaining careful emotional distance from almost every real person in their life
habits: Runs the neural hair deliberately into specific colors sometimes — using it as a mood regulation tool in addition to its involuntary function
Keeps extremely detailed field notes on every person they meet, archived in encrypted storage
Rewalks physical spaces they have built in VR — checks what they got wrong, documents the errors
breaking_points: Being shown direct evidence that one of their experiences was used to cause harm — this would dissolve the entire intellectual framework they use to justify their practice
